medications.name: Tiotropium Bromide 18 MCG Inhalation Capsule
medications.sig: Inhale contents of 1 capsule once daily

medications.name: Fluticasone-Salmeterol 250-50 MCG/ACT Inhalation Aerosol Powder Breath Activated
medications.sig: Inhale 1 puff twice daily, rinse mouth after use

medications.name: Furosemide 40 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

medications.name: Lisinopril 20 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily

medications.name: amLODIPine Besylate 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily

medications.name: Albuterol Sulfate HFA 108 (90 Base) MCG/ACT Inhalation Aerosol Solution
medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath

history.majorEvents: COPD exacerbation hospitalizations 01/2025 and 02/2026. Right knee arthroscopy 2010. PFTs 03/2026: FEV1 38% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.52 (GOLD 3, severe). Echo 2025: EF 55%, grade II diastolic dysfunction. Home oxygen 2 L/min via nasal cannula with exertion and sleep since 05/2023; portable oxygen concentrator.
history.ongoingProblems: Severe COPD with chronic hypoxic respiratory failure on home O2; heart failure with preserved EF; hypertension; bilateral knee osteoarthritis. Two falls in past 12 months.
history.social: Former smoker, 45 pack-years, quit 2014. Retired Metrobus mechanic. Lives alone in a 2nd-floor apartment (14 stairs, no elevator); daughter checks in weekly. Uses rollator walker and portable oxygen outside the home. Nearest bus stop is 3 blocks away; nearest Metrorail station is 0.8 miles.

encounters.chiefComplaint: COPD and CHF follow-up; needs MetroAccess paratransit form
encounters.subjective:
73 y/o M with severe COPD on home oxygen, HFpEF and bilateral knee OA. Dyspnea mMRC grade 3: stops for breath after walking about 100 yards or a few minutes on level ground.
Cannot walk the 3 blocks to the bus stop without stopping 2-3 times; cannot stand more than 5-10 minutes waiting for a bus or train. Knee pain limits walking and stairs. Two falls in the past year.
Cold air, hot humid days and poor air-quality days trigger exacerbations. Afraid of falling on ice and snow with walker and oxygen tank. Furosemide causes urinary urgency for several hours each morning.
Can travel without a personal care attendant if door-to-door transportation is available.
encounters.objective:
O2 sat 91% at rest on room air, 85% after 50 feet of ambulation, 94% on 2 L/min. Lungs: diminished breath sounds, prolonged expiration, scattered expiratory wheezes. CV: RRR, 1+ bilateral ankle edema.
MSK: bilateral knee crepitus, reduced flexion. Gait slow and wide-based with rollator walker; requires rest after 50 feet.
encounters.assessment:
Severe COPD, GOLD 3 (J44.9) with chronic hypoxic respiratory failure on home O2 (J96.11).
Chronic diastolic heart failure (I50.32).
Hypertension (I10), on treatment.
Bilateral primary knee osteoarthritis (M17.0).
Disability is long-term; no expectation of improvement. Unable to independently use fixed-route Metrobus/Metrorail due to limited walking distance, oxygen dependence, fall risk and environmental triggers.
encounters.plan:
Continue tiotropium, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol PRN, furosemide, lisinopril, amlodipine. Oxygen 2 L/min with exertion and sleep.
Requires rollator walker and portable oxygen for all travel.
Able to complete a functional assessment if BP does not exceed 180/110 and he may use his oxygen and walker.
Complete WMATA MetroAccess Part B. Pulmonary rehab referral. Follow-up 3 months.
